name: Bali Bali
variant: Bali Ha'i at the Beach, New Orleans (Berry)
venue: Bali Ha'i at the Beach (Pontchartrain Beach)
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007) / Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
notes: A four-spirit punch (dark and light rum, gin, cognac) from the Polynesian restaurant at New Orleans' Pontchartrain Beach amusement park; structurally a Scorpion cousin that swaps orgeat for passion fruit syrup and falernum. Two independent transcriptions of Berry's spec agree on the 1 oz-each build.

name: Scorpion
variant: Kelbo's (Hank Riddle), Los Angeles, 1950s — single serving
creator: Hank Riddle
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Kelbo's individual-sized answer to the Scorpion Bowl: passion fruit syrup joins the orgeat, the rum is dark Jamaican instead of light Puerto Rican, and a little gin backs the cognac. Both transcriptions checked agree.

name: Polynesian Guava Daiquiri
creator: Hank Riddle
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
garnish: maraschino cherry and pineapple chunk on a pick
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Neither Polynesian nor a daiquiri: a gin sour made with guava nectar and a spoon of crème de banane, flash-blended. A Hank Riddle house specialty at Kelbo's.

name: Cherie Valentino
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007) — Berry's reconstruction
notes: A communal bowl for two served at Kelbo's from the 1950s to the 1980s. A magazine feature listed only the ingredients, so the proportions are Berry's reconstruction, not a recovered spec: a sweet-tart red gin punch with blackberry and grenadine.

name: Sweet Dream
creator: Hank Riddle
location: Fairfax Avenue, Los Angeles, California, USA
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A small creamy dessert drink Hank Riddle made in his final year at Kelbo's: cacao, banana and pineapple with cream and a little light rum, dusted with nutmeg. Closer to a Golden Cadillac than to a sour.

name: Tiger Shark

ingredients.orig: blended lightly aged rum (Smuggler's Cove category, per transcription)
blended aged rum (Smuggler's Cove category, per transcription)

glass: small tumbler (original China Trader specialty glass)
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007), from bartender Tony Ramos's notebook
notes: From the China Trader, where the Hawaiian Eye TV crew drank: a three-rum pineapple daiquiri blended for a few seconds and strained. Proportions are from Berry; the rum categories come from a Smuggler's Cove-style transcription, so exact bottlings may differ.

name: Hawaiian Eye
creator: Tony Ramos
glass: Hawaiian Eye mug or old fashioned
source: Tony Ramos recipe as transcribed by TikiBot; cross-checked against Difford's Guide and Mixing Up Tiki (listed in Berry's Total Tiki)
notes: Made by Tony Ramos at the China Trader for the cast of the TV series Hawaiian Eye and served in a now-collectible mug: a simple falernum daiquiri on gold and light rum. Published versions differ on the lime and the rum split (Difford's adds more falernum and uses rich syrup; Mixing Up Tiki uses 1.5 oz of one rum and 0.75 oz lime).

name: Golden Wave
creator: Jose 'Joe' Yatco
source: Difford's Guide (adapted spec); also listed in Berry's Total Tiki
notes: Joe Yatco's 1969 China Trader creation: light rum with orange liqueur and falernum over pineapple and lemon, blended with crushed ice. The proportions are Difford's adaptation and were not checked against Berry's printed version.

name: Heavens Above
source: Difford's Guide, adapted from Jeff Berry's Intoxica! (2002)
notes: A Canadian entry in Intoxica!: a long rum-and-pineapple drink with small amounts of chocolate and coffee liqueur. Difford's dates it to about 1970 at the Top of Toronto, but places that restaurant in the CN Tower, which opened in 1976, so the date is unclear.

name: Aloha Cocktail
creator: Hank Riddle
venue: Don the Beachcomber, Palm Springs (competition entry)
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Hank Riddle's entry in a 1970 cocktail competition, made (per the transcription) while he tended bar at the Palm Springs Don the Beachcomber: a served-up rum sour tinted with grenadine and Danish cherry wine and fortified with 151. It was a competition drink, not a Beachcomber menu item.

name: Kamehameha Rum Punch
garnish: pineapple chunk speared to a cherry
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A pineapple-led rum punch from the Kona hotel, with only a teaspoon each of grenadine, syrup and blackberry brandy. The dark Jamaican rum is floated, so the first sips are rum-heavy.

name: Sleeping Giant
variant: Lagoon Cocktail Terrace, Coco Palms, Kauai
venue: Lagoon Cocktail Terrace, Coco Palms Resort
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Named for the Sleeping Giant ridge behind the Coco Palms resort: an orange-pineapple rum cooler with a dash of orgeat. The original's sweet-and-sour mix is split into equal lemon and simple syrup, following our convention.

name: Pahoehoe
variant: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
venue: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
glass: double old fashioned or small tiki bowl
garnish: spent lemon shell with a sugar cube, doused with 151 and lit
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Named for smooth ropy lava, this Mauna Kea Beach Hotel drink is a tart passion fruit and grenadine rum sour served with a flaming lemon shell. It is recorded as unsweetened passion fruit juice, which the full ounce of grenadine balances.

name: Mauna Kea Kiaha
variant: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel
venue: Batik Bar, Mauna Kea Beach Hotel

ingredients.orig: light rum (transcribed as blended lightly aged rum)

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); cross-checked with Make and Drink
notes: A citrus-free coconut-and-coffee blender drink from the Mauna Kea Beach Hotel: sweetened and unsweetened coconut with coffee liqueur and light rum. A Make and Drink adaptation uses slightly more cream of coconut and less rum.

name: Tapa Punch
variant: Royal Kona Resort recipe cards (Hilton standard)

ingredients.orig: dark Jamaican rum (transcribed as black pot still rum)
sweet & sour mix (about 3 oz, inferred from transcription), split
sweet & sour mix (about 3 oz, inferred from transcription), split

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007 / 2017 edition)
notes: One of the recipe cards Royal Kona beverage director Jeff Isbister found in 2008, believed to be a Hilton house standard carried over from Harry Yee's Hawaiian Village. A big punch heavy on dark rum, with peach brandy. The original sweet-and-sour amount is inferred from the one transcription we could check.

name: Chimp in Orbit
variant: Royal Kona Resort recipe cards (Hilton standard)

ingredients.orig: lemon juice as transcribed (may stand in for sweet & sour)

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007 / 2017 edition)
notes: The name points to the 1961 chimpanzee space flights (hence the circa-1961 date); found among the Royal Kona's old recipe cards. It pairs sweet vermouth and crème de cacao with orange and lemon, which is unusual. Transcriptions disagree on the grenadine, and the large lemon amount may originally have been sweet-and-sour mix.

name: Lovely Lovely
creator: "Danny" (Papeete Bar bartender)
venue: Papeete Bar, Tahitian Lanai, Waikikian Hotel

ingredients.orig: 2 tablespoons brown sugar (another transcription says 2 teaspoons)

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A frappé 151-proof rum sour with brown sugar and curaçao from the Waikikian Hotel's Tahitian Lanai. Transcriptions disagree on the sugar (2 tablespoons vs 2 teaspoons); tablespoons is used because 2 teaspoons would leave two ounces of citrus almost unsweetened.

name: Halekulani Cocktail
variant: House Without a Key, Halekulani Hotel
venue: House Without a Key, Halekulani Hotel
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 61
notes: The circa-1930s house cocktail of the Halekulani's beachfront lounge: a bourbon sour softened with orange and pineapple and tinted with grenadine. It was sometimes made with okolehao instead. Versions differ on the small syrup additions; this follows Smuggler's Cove.

name: Captain's Grog
variant: Hukilau Room, Captain's Inn, Long Beach, c. 1962 (Berry)
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 65 (3/4 oz of each rum, flash-blended)
notes: A three-rum grog from the Captain's Inn in Long Beach, unusual for sweetening with maple syrup and adding drops of vanilla and almond extract to the falernum and curaçao. Smuggler's Cove cuts each rum to 3/4 oz and batches the modifiers as a 'Captain's Mix'.

name: Merciless Virgin
creator: Frank 'Skipper' Kent
garnish: three maraschino cherries on a pick
source: Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 67, from the Jacqueline Zumwalt collection
notes: An unpublished recipe from Skipper Kent's San Francisco bar (date unknown, between 1942 and 1967), kept in Jacqueline Zumwalt's collection and printed by Smuggler's Cove: a light-rum lemon sour with Cherry Heering, falernum, a little dry curaçao and a splash of soda. One transcription gives 3/4 oz curaçao; two give 1/4 oz.

name: Tradewinds
garnish: lemon wedge with an inside-out cocktail umbrella
source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 94
notes: A 1970s Caribbean drink Berry revived: apricot liqueur and cream of coconut balanced by a full ounce of lemon over dark and light rum. Smuggler's Cove notes that 2 oz of gin can replace the rums; Anders Erickson uses 1 oz cream of coconut.

name: Boo Loo

ingredients.orig: 2 1/2 oz pineapple juice + 6 muddled 1-inch fresh pineapple chunks (~1 1/2 oz)

source: Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 249, after Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010)
notes: A circa-1965 party drink of unstated origin served in a hollowed-out pineapple with two straws: muddled fresh pineapple, honey and lime under four rums. The rum categories are Smuggler's Cove's.

name: Tiki Bowl
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 68 (1 oz honey, 2 dashes Herbstura)
notes: A Kon-Tiki original that copies Donn Beach's signature honey, Pernod and Angostura combination across three rums with orange and lime. The Kon-Tiki chain came from Stephen Crane's 1958 deal with Sheraton to compete with Hilton's Trader Vic's.

name: Cobra
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: The Kon-Tiki chain's stripped-down relative of Don the Beachcomber's Cobra's Fang: one ounce of 151-proof Demerara rum with lime, orange, passion fruit, Pernod and bitters, flash-blended.

name: Kon-Tiki Mai Tai
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: Shows how loosely 'Mai Tai' was used in the 1960s: the Kon-Tiki version shares only rum and lime with Trader Vic's. It uses Donn Beach's honey, orange, ginger, Pernod and Angostura template instead.

name: Lady of Singapore
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A pink, creamy blender drink from the Portland Kon-Tiki: gold rum, pineapple, cream of coconut and half-and-half, sharpened with lime and tinted with grenadine. A colada relative made with dairy.

name: Samoan Typhoon
variant: Hawaiian Village Motel & Restaurant, Tampa (bowl for two)
creator: Joe King Sui

ingredients.orig: 1 oz honey dissolved in the lime juice

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A big blended punch for two from a Tampa Polynesian motel restaurant: lots of lime and passion fruit sweetened with honey, with a vodka boost on top of the rums.

name: Cou-Cou-Comber
creator: Joe Scialom

ingredients.orig: served in a hollowed-out cucumber, eaten as you drink

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A novelty from Joe Scialom (of Suffering Bastard fame) from his time at Hilton's Caribbean hotels: a Pernod-scented vodka sour poured into a hollowed-out cucumber that you eat as you drink.

name: Hot Zombie
source: Ron Rico rum company recipe booklet, via Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007)
notes: A cold-weather version from a Puerto Rican rum brand's promotional booklet: the Zombie's rum, lime, pineapple and passion fruit topped with boiling water and enriched with butter and brown sugar, like a fruity hot buttered rum.

name: Hawaiian Room
variant: Hotel Lexington, New York (Saucier, Bottoms Up, 1951)
location: New York City, New York, USA
source: Ted Saucier, Bottoms Up (1951); reprinted in Jeff Berry's Grog Log (1998)
notes: The signature of Manhattan's Hawaiian Room, the Hotel Lexington's hula-show supper club from 1937 to 1966: an up cocktail of rum with applejack, triple sec, pineapple and lemon. East Coast 'Hawaiian' rather than Beachcomber style; 1951 is the publication date.

name: Pieces of Eight
variant: Pieces of Eight restaurant, Marina del Rey, early 1960s

ingredients.orig: rum (one source says aged, another light)

source: Jeff Berry, Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010), as summarized by the Cocktail Party app; cross-checked with TikiBot's recipe table
notes: The house drink of a pirate-themed Marina del Rey restaurant in the early 1960s. As transcribed it is a Hurricane-style passion fruit sour; the rum style and whether Berry's spec has more ingredients could not be checked against the book.

name: Lei Lani Volcano
location: Walt Disney World, Lake Buena Vista, Florida, USA
source: Disney Polynesian Village Resort recipe via Make and Drink; original described in Smuggler's Cove (2016) p. 94 (Lei Lani Volcano 2.0)
notes: The 1970s house drink at Walt Disney World's Polynesian resort: coconut rum and guava nectar with pineapple and lime. Smuggler's Cove later rebuilt it as the Lei Lani Volcano 2.0 with aged rum, cream of coconut and guava soda.

name: Navy Grog
creator: Thomas Mario (published version)
source: Thomas Mario, Playboy's Host & Bar Book (1971), via Make and Drink
notes: A magazine-era Navy Grog with no honey or grapefruit, built on orange, pineapple, guava syrup and falernum instead. It shows how far the name had drifted from Don the Beachcomber's original by the early 1970s.

name: Navy Grog
location: Walt Disney World, Lake Buena Vista, Florida, USA
source: Cooking With Mickey Around the World (Disney cookbook), via Make and Drink
notes: The Polynesian resort's house Navy Grog stays closer to Don's template (honey, grapefruit, lime, soda) but uses just two rums plus a 151 kick. The creation date is unknown; the recipe comes from a Disney cookbook.

name: Silver Seas
variant: Mr. Lemon Hart's Tropical Treat booklet

ingredients.orig: Lemon Hart dark rum (transcribed as black blended rum)

source: Mr. Lemon Hart's Tropical Treat (Lemon Hart rum promotional booklet), via Make and Drink
notes: From a Lemon Hart rum promotional booklet: a short Beachcomber-style drink with Passionola (a commercial passion fruit syrup), orange and lime, and heavy dashes of both bitters and Pernod. The booklet's date wasn't confirmed, so the era is a best guess.

name: Hitler's Jitters
variant: Café Plaza, Maracaibo (Potions of the Caribbean)
creator: F. García Bode
source: Jeff Berry, Potions of the Caribbean (2013), via Make and Drink
notes: A WWII-era Venezuelan daiquiri variant from Berry's Potions of the Caribbean, flavored with crème de cacao. The 3 oz rum pour comes from a single adaptation and wasn't checked against the book.

name: Dorado Beachcomber
variant: Dorado Beach Hotel, Puerto Rico (Berry adaptation)
source: Dorado Beach Hotel recipe as adapted by Jeff Berry, via Mixing Up Tiki
notes: A Mai Tai-shaped house drink from the Dorado Beach Hotel in Puerto Rico, built on lemon rather than lime, with orgeat, curaçao and demerara syrup over an overproof and an aged rum. Known only through Berry's adaptation; the exact rums are uncertain.

variant: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation, Kauai (early 1960s)
venue: House of Happy Talk lounge, Hanalei Plantation

ingredients.orig: part of 2 oz Hanalei house mix (3 lemon : 1 orgeat : 1 guava : 1 orange : 1 pineapple : 1/4 passion : 1/4 simple)

glass: 15 oz brandy snifter or hollowed-out pineapple
garnish: pineapple chunk and cherry on a spear
source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007), from the California Bartenders Guild's Good Taste; house-mix breakdown per seezee's Teekee Deebee
notes: Named for the South Pacific song (the lounge was the House of Happy Talk): light rum and a juicy lemon-orgeat house mix topped with Champagne, sometimes made with okolehao. The house-mix breakdown comes from one transcription; a Make and Drink version uses plain lime-lemon sour mix with rum and okolehao. Different drink from the San Diego Bali Hai's Mr. Bali Hai.

variant: House of Happy Talk, Hanalei Plantation, Kauai (early 1960s)
venue: House of Happy Talk lounge, Hanalei Plantation

ingredients.orig: 2 level tbsp diced fresh pineapple, blended
2 level tbsp diced fresh banana, blended

source: Jeff Berry, Sippin' Safari (2007); house-mix breakdown per seezee's Teekee Deebee
notes: The House of Happy Talk's liquefied fruit punch: fresh pineapple and banana blended with the lemon-orgeat house mix, curaçao and light rum, poured over ice, swizzled, and topped with a spoon of dark rum. The house-mix breakdown comes from one transcription.

name: Beachcomber
variant: Official Mixer's Manual (Duffy, 1956 ed.) — not Don the Beachcomber's
source: Patrick Gavin Duffy, The Official Mixer's Manual (1956 edition), as adapted by Difford's Guide
notes: Not a Don the Beachcomber recipe: a Cuban-style daiquiri variant sweetened only with triple sec and a touch of maraschino, from mid-century bar manuals. Difford's lists an optional half teaspoon of rich syrup, left out here.

name: Pago Pago
variant: The How and When (c. 1940) via Berry's Remixed
source: Beachbum Berry Remixed (2010), after Gale & Marco's The How and When (c. 1940), as adapted by Difford's Guide
notes: A pre-war pineapple daiquiri accented with green Chartreuse and white crème de cacao; Berry traces it to a c. 1940 bar book rather than to Trader Vic. Sources disagree on the liqueurs (0.5/0.5 at Difford's; Anders Erickson uses 1/4 oz Chartreuse and 1/2 oz cacao; a Ronrico booklet version reverses that).

name: Zamboanga 'Zeinie'
variant: Charles H. Baker Jr., The Gentleman's Companion (1939)
source: Charles H. Baker Jr., The Gentleman's Companion Vol. II (1939), as adapted by Difford's Guide
notes: One of Baker's colonial-Pacific finds, which he said travelled down the islands from Manila to Mindanao: a brandy sour with pineapple syrup, maraschino and bitters. Difford's adaptation adds saline, left out here; Baker's original amounts weren't checked.

name: Rum Barrel
variant: Steve Crane (Luau / Kon-Tiki) — per Make and Drink recreation
creator: Stephen Crane (attributed)

ingredients.orig: light rum (transcribed as blended lightly aged)
dark Jamaican rum (transcribed as black blended, Jamaica)

source: Make and Drink recreation ('Steve's Rum Barrel'); Berry's Total Tiki lists a 'Rum Barrel (Steve Crane)'
notes: A Rum Barrel attributed by name to Stephen Crane of the Luau and the Kon-Tiki chain: 4 oz of light and dark rum over four juices, sweetened with honey and passion fruit and dashed with Angostura. Known here only from one video recreation, so the attribution and proportions are unconfirmed.

name: Rum & Fruit
source: Ron Rico Official Mixers' Guide (rum company booklet), via Make and Drink
notes: A rum-company booklet daiquiri variant with Bénédictine and a little passion fruit syrup; an early example of an herbal liqueur used with tropical fruit. The booklet's date and exact wording weren't checked.
